name: default
description: Literature- and assumption-based defaults for the contention simulator. Every value is either cited in 'sources' or marked as an assumption there. Results produced from this file are simulated, not measured.

aidev-upper.note: Upper scenario: per-file rate chosen so pairs that share a file conflict about 40% of the time, the cross-agent co-active pair rate of Xu et al. (41.7%). Treated as an upper bound, not a default (orchestrator guidance 2026-10-03).

intra-agent.note: Pairs from one agent (Xu et al. 19.8%) applied to file-sharing pairs.

brun-high-semantic.note: Semantic breaks near the top of Brun et al.'s 3-28% of merges followed by test failures.

pair_conflict_rate.source: step-1 preliminary measurements, 600 sampled pairs within 20 changes per corpus (orchestrator message 2026-10-03)

file_sharing_pair_share.source: local measurement of data/<corpus>/corpus.jsonl while building this model

cursor_lock_collapse.target: 20 agents slow to the throughput of 1-3 with locks
cursor_lock_collapse.check: experiments.py 'lock-collapse' rows: beanstalk with placement_fallback=wait at N=20

sources.test_minutes: 10-minute CI: lhorie's merge-queue arithmetic (HN 36708767), 'CI of 10 min gives a budget of 6 serial merges/hour' (docs/claude-02 section B1). Chromium CQ's median under 40 min is a slower reference.
sources.ci_slots: Assumption from the study brief: R = max(2, N/10); experiments.py adds a fixed-R variant to show CI saturation. At N = 1,000, R = 100 jobs stays under the Cloudflare account cap of 1,500 vCPU, about 375-750 jobs (docs/claude-opus/01-evidence.md section 4).
sources.flake_rate: Assumption (study brief default 2%). Flakes are first-order at scale: Chromium has about 20,000 flaky tests and retries failed shards (docs/claude-02 section B1).
sources.p_self: Study brief default 15% per change version. Together with semantic breaks and conflicts it gives the simulated main-branch failure rate of roughly 25-30%, close to CircleCI's main-branch success rate of 70.8% (2026 State of Software Delivery; docs/claude-02 section A4).
sources.work_time: Assumption: lognormal, median 20 min, sigma 0.7 (study brief: median 20 min). AIDev's median review turnaround for accepted Codex PRs is 0.3 h (arXiv 2507.15003; docs/claude-02 section A1).
sources.r_conf_r_fix: Study brief defaults: rework after a conflict 0.3x, fix after a red 0.4x the original work time (assumption).
sources.p_per_file: Per shared non-dissolvable file, so P(conflict) = 1 - (1 - p)^shared_files compounds with overlap. 0.06 reproduces step 1's preliminary ~9-13% conflict rate given a shared file and ~1% pairwise rate (orchestrator message 2026-10-03). The literature's 41.7% cross-agent rate (Xu et al., arXiv 2607.04697, 115 co-active cross-agent pairs), 19.8% intra-agent rate and AgenticFlict's 27.67% of 107k agent PRs (arXiv 2604.03551) are co-active-pair or per-PR rates in small repos; they are kept as the 'aidev-upper' and 'intra-agent' scenarios, not the default.
sources.p_per_file_diss: Assumption: lockfile and changelog edits collide often (0.3 per shared file) but merge drivers dissolve them. Xu et al.: 84.4% of conflicted files are source files, so at most ~15.6% of conflicts are in other categories; diss_file_share = 0.1 marks 10% of files dissolvable.
sources.p_module: Assumption: shared module, no shared file. Textual conflicts need a shared path, so this only covers renames and moves (Xu et al.: 26.8% of conflict reports are modify/delete). Step 1 measures it.
sources.merge_drivers: On for every policy (thesis section 2: commutative merge drivers for hot files).
sources.q_sem: Unknown for real repos; swept over {0, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2} by experiments.py. Default 0.01 per co-active pair that shares a non-commutative module. Anchors: Uber SubmitQueue (EuroSys'19) reports a 40% mainline-break probability with 16 concurrent potentially conflicting changes, i.e. 0.4-3.3% per pair depending on whether all 120 pairs or one change's 15 partners are meant; Brun et al. (FSE 2011, 3,562 merges) saw test failures after 3-28% of merges. With 37% of co-active pairs sharing a module, q_sem = 0.01 breaks about 7% of changes against 19 concurrent predecessors.
sources.dependency_rate: Assumption 5%: share of tasks that need an earlier task (within 20) in their base. Step 1 measures it (dependency_rate).
sources.recall_precision: Module-level placement only (placement_model=module): module recall 0.8, precision 0.6, assumed. Step 2 measures micro recall 0.47-0.58 at the F1-optimal threshold (title only).
sources.commit_round: Assumption: a committer or queue merge round costs 10 s plus 1 s per change. The thesis's illustrative model assumes about one change per 3 s round (docs/claude-opus/02 section 4). The same mechanical step is charged to the queue's candidate build.
sources.batching: bors-ng bisects failed batches in halves; Mergify splits failed batches and fills batches by priority; GitHub's merge queue groups 1-100 PRs (docs/claude-02 section B1). batch_k = 4 is the default; experiments.py sweeps k over {1, 4, 16}.
sources.aimd: Zuul's dependent pipeline window starts at 20, grows by one per successful merge and halves per failure (docs/claude-02 section B1). Here the AIMD variant adapts the batch size k (start 4, +1 per green batch, halve per red, range 1-32).
sources.spec_depth: Speculative train depth min(R, 20). GitLab merge trains default to 20 parallel pipelines per train; GitHub's merge queue allows build concurrency 1-100 (docs/claude-02 section B1).
sources.queue_agents: Study brief: in the queue the author agent stays bound to its PR until it lands and handles ejections. 'released' is a fairness variant (authors move on; ejections become tickets for any free agent).
sources.requeue: A good queue keeps an ejected PR's position (front), so the PR is re-tested soon after rework rather than after the whole queue.
sources.budget: Error budget B = 3 open reds, A = 30 min (thesis section 3, step 7: 'at most 3 open reds, none older than 30 minutes').
sources.a_suspect: Assumption 0.7: the read/write-set suspect set contains the true culprit. The thesis leaves this untested (section 7, 'Read sets are noisy').
sources.snapshot: Thesis section 2: each task runs on a fork of the fast trunk at T0 (head). 'green' (fork from the newest validated commit) is the thesis's answer to red-trunk poisoning (section 7) and a sensitivity row.
sources.green_mode: prefix is the study brief: green moves to a fast-trunk commit whose full suite passed. quarantine is an extension (not in the brief): green moves to the tested head minus known culprits and the commits built on them, as a queue's ejection would.
sources.placement: Pair-level placement (default; orchestrator guidance 2026-10-03 after step 2): when candidate t is checked against a held task r, the pair is flagged with probability flag_recall if it would textually conflict under the interaction model, otherwise with probability flag_clean (one latent draw per pair). Hard placement (placement_fallback=wait) never starts a flagged task; soft (least-overlap, the default) takes the task with the fewest flags, so no agent idles. Default operating point 'predicted-typical' (0.60, 0.25). flag_points are the measured step-2 operating points at conflict recall 0.60: codex title+body clean-flag 0.15 (best case), workers-sdk directory-level kNN 0.21 and platform 0.29 (typical); the module-level combined predictor at its tuned threshold flags 0.87-0.93 of conflicting and 0.53-0.90 of clean pairs; a file-level oracle flags all conflicting and 0.04-0.06 of clean pairs; 'hot-file-rule' (0.30, 0.02) is an ASSUMED scenario that serialises only the few files that dominate conflicts (in platform one file has 31% of conflicting pairs). Module-level placement on perturbed module sets (placement_model=module, spec's rho/pi model) is kept as a variant; step 2 found module footprints too coarse to place on (a perfect module oracle still flags 33-74% of clean pairs).
sources.review: Human review is excluded from both policies: modelling it only for the queue would hand Beanstalk an advantage the baseline could also take (Duckbill's unreviewed lane merges in 1 h against 26 h; Pragmatic Engineer 2026-09-08, docs/claude-opus/01-evidence.md finding 2).
sources.footprint: Parametric fallback tuned to the local public corpora (data/codex, data/workers-sdk): 2.5 modules and 4.5 files per module per change, Zipf module popularity, popular modules larger, Zipf file popularity (s = 1.0) inside modules. See sanity_targets for the pair statistics it implies.
